posts.content:
The failure mode isn't inaccuracy, it's invisible inaccuracy.

That's the core argument in the second installment of The RWE Standard, our monthly column on HEOR and real-world evidence in the age of AI, written by Ashis Das.

Validating AI in health research used to mean one thing: train it, test it, measure performance. That worked when AI produced a single, fixed output. Now AI reasons through a chain of decisions, and that old paradigm doesn't cover it.

In this piece, Ashis breaks down why the old paradigm can't catch this new failure mode (hint: the output can look completely right and still be wrong), and lays out what validating a reasoning chain actually requires.

Read the full piece: https://lnkd.in/gKErF2fR

#HEOR #RealWorldEvidence #AI

posts.content:
An AI method applied to bad data doesn't produce uncertain evidence. It produces confidently wrong evidence.

That's the core argument in the first installment of The RWE Standard, our new monthly column on HEOR and real-world evidence in the age of AI, written by Ashis Das, MD, MPH, PhD.

AI adoption in HEOR has moved from experimentation to operational reality. Literature review, causal inference, health economic modeling, all of it faster than ever. But speed and credibility are not the same argument, and only one of them has been made so far.

In this piece, Ashis breaks down where the real gap sits. Hint: it's not the algorithm. And he makes the case for building validation in now, because the teams that do will be the ones still standing when the reckoning arrives.

Read the full piece: https://lnkd.in/d5ZnVfnV

#HEOR #RealWorldEvidence #AI

A team building an in-house AI analytics tool isn't a few weeks behind Marmot. It's more than a year behind.

That's the real timeline behind our latest piece, written by John W., Head of Revenue Strategy at Komodo Health.

Almost every Marmot customer tried building their own AI-based analytics solution first. A small team, a foundational model, a few weeks, and a demo that looks great on a Zoom call. That part's easy. It's also where the real work starts, not ends.

In this piece, John breaks down what actually separates a working demo from a platform healthcare can rely on, and why Komodo's own path from MVP to trustworthy product took 16 months, not four weeks. Hint: the gap isn't the model. It's everything healthcare requires around it.

Read the full article to see what it takes to build AI that healthcare can rely on: https://lnkd.in/gXhUWhJC
